items.title: Home sales fall as prices keep rising
items.body: Spain's home sales fell 13.4% year on year in September, while prices rose 14.7% year on year in Q3. Fotocasa research director María Matos says higher prices and interest rates are shrinking the pool of buyers. Sales fell most sharply in País Vasco, Baleares, and Madrid.

items.title: Approved wage rises face pressure from inflation
items.body: The government approved Royal Decrees that would raise the SMI (minimum wage) by 5.3% to €1,286 a month in 2027 and civil servant pay by 4.5%. It also approved pay transparency rules. Forecast average pay rises of 3.5-4.2% would lag October's 4.9% inflation.

items.title: Sánchez rules out Catalonia referendum after election
items.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said on November 22 that he would not allow a Catalan self-determination referendum, even if he needs votes from Junts or ERC to govern. The general election is on November 29.

items.title: Feijóo sets terms for possible Vox coalition
items.body: PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has set conditions for a possible coalition with Vox after the November 29 election. These include experienced ministers and respect for Spain's autonomous communities. He has accepted that he will probably need Vox to govern.

items.title: Fitch sees little room for tax cuts
items.body: Ratings agency Fitch says Spain has limited room to cut taxes, with the public deficit forecast at 2.3% in 2026. It expects growth to remain more than double Europe's rate for two years. Low productivity and an ageing population leave the next government facing longer-term pressures.

items.title: Living donors qualify for full-rate sick pay
items.body: Under an October 2026 Royal Decree-law, living organ and tissue donors receive sick pay at 100% of the base used to calculate benefits, versus a maximum of 75% for ordinary illness. No minimum prior contributions are required. Cover runs from preparation through recovery; blood donation is excluded.

items.title: Marc Márquez secures eighth MotoGP world title
items.body: Ducati rider Marc Márquez secured his eighth MotoGP title by finishing ninth at the Portuguese Grand Prix on November 22. It is his 10th world title overall and matches former champion Giacomo Agostini's eight top-class titles. Márquez overcame a 102-point deficit after surgery and two missed races.

items.title: Airlines warn of higher summer 2027 fares
items.body: Airlines warn of higher fares and fewer seats for summer 2027 as jet fuel costs remain high and European refining difficulties add pressure. Ryanair says fares could rise by up to 20%. Most airlines have locked in prices for only about 25% of next summer's fuel.

items.title: Madrid protesters demand small-business VAT exemption
items.body: About 600 autónomos (self-employed workers) marched in Madrid on November 22, demanding a VAT exemption for annual turnover below €85,000 and contributions based on real income. The EU exemption directive is not in force in Spain. The European Commission took Spain to the EU Court of Justice in March over the delay.

items.title: Hernández de Cos gains backing for ECB
items.body: Bank for International Settlements chief Pablo Hernández de Cos has backing from Germany, France, Italy, and Spain to lead the ECB. Confirmation could come during the week of November 23. Other euro partners are annoyed with the Franco-German push, and Dutch rival Klaas Knot has not withdrawn.

items.title: Plan Vive charges push applicant over limit
items.body: A worker earning €2,300 a month was rejected for a Plan Vive affordable rental in Arganda del Rey. Extra charges raised the advertised €736 rent to €850, or 37% of his income. The scheme caps housing costs at 35%, showing how added fees can put advertised rents out of reach.
